g-glossary-c-s.title: Glossary definitions C-S (Critical Path to Start-to-Finish): precise wordings and glossary-only facts
g-glossary-c-s.notes: Consistent with the body; items valuable for precision or found only in the glossary: data (discrete, unorganised, unprocessed measurements or raw observations) vs information (organised or structured data processed for a purpose to make it meaningful) vs knowledge (mixture of experience, values and beliefs, context, intuition and insight used to make sense of new experiences); data date (point in time when project status is recorded); decision tree analysis (diagramming and calculation technique for evaluating a chain of options under uncertainty); defect (imperfection or deficiency where a component does not meet requirements or specifications and must be repaired or replaced) and rework (action to bring a defective component into compliance); development approach (method to create and evolve the product - predictive, iterative, incremental, agile, hybrid); discrete effort (an activity that can be planned and measured and yields a specific output - glossary note: one of three EVM activity types used to measure work performance; level of effort (LOE) is another - an activity that does not produce definitive end products and is measured by the passage of time; the third type, apportioned effort, is not defined in this glossary - lessons will flag this); duration (total work periods to complete an activity, in hours, days or weeks) vs effort (labour units required) - contrast; early/late start and finish dates defined relative to network logic, data date or project completion date and constraints; earned value management (methodology combining scope, schedule and resource measurements to assess performance and progress); EEFs here say 'not under the immediate control of the team'; estimate; execute (directing, managing, performing and accomplishing work, providing deliverables and work performance information); fallback plan (alternative actions if the primary plan must be abandoned); fee (profit component of seller compensation); fixed-price contract (fee for a defined scope regardless of cost or effort); float = slack (total float and free float); forward pass; functional organisation (staff grouped by specialisation, PM has limited authority); grade (category for items with the same functional use but different quality requirements); ground rules; imposed date (fixed date, e.g., 'start no earlier than', 'finish no later than'); incentive fee; independent estimates (third party analyses information to predict cost, schedule etc.); input (any item required by a process before it proceeds, possibly a predecessor's output) and output (product, result or service generated by a process, possibly an input to a successor); invitation for bid (generally equivalent to RFP, narrower in some areas); issue (a current condition that may impact objectives) vs risk (uncertain future event or condition); lag and lead; lessons learned, register and repository; logical relationship (dependency between two activities or an activity and a milestone); management reserve (budget or schedule held outside the performance measurement baseline for management control, for unforeseen in-scope work); management skills (plan, organise, direct and control people); master schedule and milestone schedule; matrix organisation (PM shares responsibility with functional managers for priorities and directing work); methodology; milestone; monitor (collect data, produce measures, report and disseminate information) - control defined separately; Monte Carlo simulation (model iterated many times with random inputs from distributions and probabilistic branches); network logic, network path, node; opportunity (risk with a positive effect); OBS (hierarchical representation of the project organisation relating activities to performing units); organisational learning; percent complete; performance measurement baseline (integrated scope, schedule and cost baselines); performance reviews; phase gate (decision to continue, continue with modification or end a project or program); planned value; planning package (below the control account with known content but no detailed activities); plurality; policy, practice, procedure, process definitions; procurement audits (review of contracts and contracting processes for completeness, accuracy, effectiveness); procurement documents (bid and proposal documents incl. IFB, invitation for negotiations, RFI, RFQ, RFP and seller responses) vs procurement documentation (all documents used in signing, executing and closing an agreement, possibly predating the project); product (quantifiable artefact, end item or component); progressive elaboration (iteratively increasing plan detail as information and estimates improve); project funding requirements; project initiation (launching a process that can result in authorisation); project management system (aggregation of processes, tools, techniques, methodologies, resources and procedures); project management team vs project team; project team directory; quality audits, checklists, metrics, policy, report, requirement; quality management system (organisational framework of policies, processes, procedures, resources; the project quality plan should be compatible with it); RACI; regression analysis; regulations (requirements imposed by a governmental body) vs standard (established by authority, custom or general consent as a model); requirement here 'to satisfy a business need'; reserve (provision to mitigate cost and/or schedule risk, often qualified as management or contingency reserve); residual risk (risk remaining after responses are implemented); resource histogram; resource leveling (may affect the critical path) vs resource smoothing (uses free and total float without affecting the critical path); responsibility (an assignment that can be delegated, creating a duty to perform); result (outcomes and documents); risk appetite (degree of uncertainty an organisation or individual will accept in anticipation of reward); risk threshold (level of exposure above which risks are addressed and below which they may be accepted); risk exposure (aggregate measure of the potential impact of all risks at a point in time); risk category, risk owner (monitors risks and selects and implements a response), risk review (meeting examining response effectiveness), risk response definitions (acceptance, avoidance, enhancement, escalation - shifting ownership to a higher organisational level, exploiting, mitigation, sharing, transference); role; schedule model and scheduling tool; scope (sum of products, services and results); secondary risk; self-organising teams; seller proposals; service level agreement (contract between a service provider - internal or external - and the end user defining expected service level); specification and specification limits (area either side of the mean meeting customer requirements; may be wider or narrower than the control limits); sponsor (person or group providing resources and support and accountable for enabling success) and sponsoring organisation; stakeholder analysis; standard; start date; SF relationship.
